packages.label: מוֹפְתִים וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי פֶּה
packages.label_en: Miracles and Mouth-Rulings of the Posek
packages.reason: The entire Torah turns on a single bechina: the miracles performed through halachic decisors (ba'alei posekim) and the divine 'judgments of His mouth' (מִשְׁפְּטֵי פִיהוּ) are two expressions of the same thing. The Rebbe quotes I Chronicles 16:12 — 'מֹפְתָיו וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי פִיהוּ' — and uses 'בִּבְחִינַת' to equate the posek's rulings with divine wonders. It is not that rulings cause miracles (eitza) — rather, the posek's ruling IS the miracle, because his accepted authority makes them one and the same act. 'מוֹפְתִים' and 'מִשְׁפְּטֵי פִיהוּ' share the same essential nature: the divine will expressed through the authoritative mouth. Similarly, the miracles of the Geonim are a bechina of the same phenomenon — 'וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת הַמּוֹפְתִים שֶׁמְּסַפְּרִין מֵהַגְּאוֹנִים'. All three — מוֹפְתִים, מִשְׁפְּטֵי פִיהוּ, and מוֹפְתֵי הַגְּאוֹנִים — are different expressions of the one domain: divine power manifesting through the authoritative halachic voice.
